posts.text: Breathing a mix of carbon tetrafluoride and oxygen for 10 minutes before decompression from a simulated 200-foot dive reduced decompression sickness in pigs. The technique could extend the depth accessible for human exploration. In PNAS: https://ow.ly/SFsl50ZB3zr

Fast-growing wildfires tend to be stronger and burn a larger proportion of area at high severity levels, according to a new analysis of 3499 recent wildfires in the conifer forests of Canada and the western United States. 

Learn more in #ScienceAdvances: https://scim.ag/4bK33aj

posts.text: In the forests of Puerto Rico, individual trees from the same species can store, handle, and transport water in different ways based on the dryness of their respective habitats. https://scim.ag/3U1icy3
posts.external_title: Surprising uniqueness of Puerto Rico’s trees could make them more resistant to drought
posts.external_description: Two trees from the same species can vary in how they transport and manage water, improving specieswide drought resilience

posts.external_title: Cascading continental-scale floods across Europe in 1342–1343 - Nature
posts.external_description: Tracing cascading continental-scale medieval megafloods across Europe indicates that current flood management is unprepared for such sequences, highlighting the urgent need for proactive flood risk management strategies that account for unusual series of extreme flood events.
